Article 3
(1) The objective of the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
(2) Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence; and/or
c. psychological violence.

Article 3
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.
Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.
Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.
Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

Article 20
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Every person who commits acts of obstructing officers or P2TP2A institutions or any party in carrying out protection and service efforts for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(3) The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about women and children who are victims of violence as well as laws and regulations related to women and children who are victims of violence;
b. implementing education about anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. implementing socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence;
d. implementing monitoring and evaluation of the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Regional Government...
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and ensuring the operation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements;
b. facilitating the formation of service institutions;
c. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to ensure the implementation of protection for victims by taking into account the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons legally.
(4) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to supervise the implementation of services for victims, with service standards that involve the community.
(5) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide funds for the protection of women and children victims of violence through the APBD as well as other sources that are legal and non-binding.
(6) The Regent appoints an Official to carry out the obligations and responsibilities of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person who is female by sex.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection...
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the matter and according to the manner regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her civilly.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family...
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with laws and regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor about matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Doctor specializing in Psychiatry about the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 16
(1) Guidance on the implementation of protection for women and children shall be carried out by relevant Agencies in accordance with their respective main duties and functions.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of providing guidelines that include technical implementation of protection for women and children.
(3) Supervision...
(3) Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children shall be carried out by relevant Agencies together with government internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:

(2) Regional Government...
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and ensuring the operation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements;
b. facilitating the formation of service institutions;

(5) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide funds for the protection of women and children victims of violence through the APBD as well as other sources that are legal and non-binding.
(6) The Regent appoints an Official to carry out the obligations and responsibilities of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:

CONCERNING

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

(1) The objective of the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
(2) Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person who is female by sex.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection...
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the matter and according to the manner regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her civilly.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family...
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with laws and regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor about matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Doctor specializing in Psychiatry about the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 20
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Every person who commits acts of obstructing officers or P2TP2A institutions or any party in carrying out protection and service efforts for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(3) The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

BAB II
PRINCIPLES, OBJECTIVES, AND SERVICE PRINCIPLES
Pasal 2
Protection of women and children victims of violence is implemented based on the principles of:
a. Respect and fulfillment of victims' rights; b. Justice and gender equality;
c. Non-discrimination;
d. Best interests of victims.

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about women and children who are victims of violence as well as laws and regulations related to women and children who are victims of violence;
b. implementing education about anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. implementing socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence;
d. implementing monitoring and evaluation of the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Regional Government...
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and ensuring the operation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements;
b. facilitating the formation of service institutions;
c. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to ensure the implementation of protection for victims by taking into account the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons legally.
(4) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to supervise the implementation of services for victims, with service standards that involve the community.
(5) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide funds for the protection of women and children victims of violence through the APBD as well as other sources that are legal and non-binding.
(6) The Regent appoints an Official to carry out the obligations and responsibilities of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 11
(1) The principle of service provision to victims is not subject to any fees whatsoever.
(2) The provision of services to victims is carried out quickly, safely, with empathy, and non-discriminatory.
(3) Services to victims regarding everything that is reported are guaranteed confidentiality.

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person who is female by sex.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection...
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the matter and according to the manner regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her civilly.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family...
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with laws and regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor about matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Doctor specializing in Psychiatry about the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 3
(1) The objective of the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
(2) Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence; and/or
c. psychological violence.

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about women and children who are victims of violence as well as laws and regulations related to women and children who are victims of violence;
b. implementing education about anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. implementing socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence;
d. implementing monitoring and evaluation of the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Regional Government...
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and ensuring the operation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements;
b. facilitating the formation of service institutions;
c. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to ensure the implementation of protection for victims by taking into account the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons legally.
(4) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to supervise the implementation of services for victims, with service standards that involve the community.
(5) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide funds for the protection of women and children victims of violence through the APBD as well as other sources that are legal and non-binding.
(6) The Regent appoints an Official to carry out the obligations and responsibilities of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 20
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Every person who commits acts of obstructing officers or P2TP2A institutions or any party in carrying out protection and service efforts for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(3) The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

Article 3
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.
Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.
Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.
Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person who is female by sex.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection...
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the matter and according to the manner regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her civilly.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family...
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with laws and regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor about matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Doctor specializing in Psychiatry about the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 3
(1) The objective of the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
(2) Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence; and/or
c. psychological violence.

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about women and children who are victims of violence as well as laws and regulations related to women and children who are victims of violence;
b. implementing education about anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. implementing socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence;
d. implementing monitoring and evaluation of the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Regional Government...
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and ensuring the operation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements;
b. facilitating the formation of service institutions;
c. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to ensure the implementation of protection for victims by taking into account the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons legally.
(4) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to supervise the implementation of services for victims, with service standards that involve the community.
(5) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide funds for the protection of women and children victims of violence through the APBD as well as other sources that are legal and non-binding.
(6) The Regent appoints an Official to carry out the obligations and responsibilities of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 20
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Every person who commits acts of obstructing officers or P2TP2A institutions or any party in carrying out protection and service efforts for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(3) The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

CHAPTER IX
ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 17
(1) Officials or Officers appointed by authorized institutions/agencies who fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities as regulated in Article 7 and Article 8, shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. written warning from the authorized official; and/or
b. fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Further provisions regarding the procedures for imposing administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11
(1) The principle of service provision to victims is not subject to any fees whatsoever.
(2) The provision of services to victims is carried out quickly, safely, with empathy, and non-discriminatory.
(3) Services to victims regarding everything that is reported are guaranteed confidentiality.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, firstly is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 3
(1) The objective of the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
(2) Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence; and/or
c. psychological violence.

Article 3
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.
Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.
Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.
Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

7.4.text:
CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about women and children who are victims of violence as well as laws and regulations related to women and children who are victims of violence;
b. implementing education about anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. implementing socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence;
d. implementing monitoring and evaluation of the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Regional Government...
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and ensuring the operation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements;
b. facilitating the formation of service institutions;
c. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to ensure the implementation of protection for victims by taking into account the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons legally.
(4) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to supervise the implementation of services for victims, with service standards that involve the community.
(5) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide funds for the protection of women and children victims of violence through the APBD as well as other sources that are legal and non-binding.
(6) The Regent appoints an Official to carry out the obligations and responsibilities of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person who is female by sex.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection...
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the matter and according to the manner regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her civilly.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family...
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with laws and regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor about matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Doctor specializing in Psychiatry about the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 20
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Every person who commits acts of obstructing officers or P2TP2A institutions or any party in carrying out protection and service efforts for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(3) The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.
